original_test_intent: Change the credential of one dedicated least-privilege BMC test account and verify protected authentication, rotation and recovery without exposing the secret.
original_method: Do not invent password bytes; require vendor schema, vault-generated secret, dedicated user, security approval, non-disclosing login verification, rotation/revocation and rollback.
manual_activity: Vendor/security owner defines credential semantics and approves a dedicated account; operator validates vault path and independent admin recovery.

command_applicability.command_recommendation: None until vault-backed vendor method and rollback are approved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Baseline one dedicated user, inject one generated secret through protected channel, verify login/privilege without disclosure, rotate/revoke and restore approved final credential.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds absent credential-security contract without editing Master.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Password-status/read-only checks cannot replace actual change coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong target or secret handling can cause lockout or credential compromise.

project_override_considerations: Any tool must keep secrets out of visible arguments/evidence and provide equivalent user targeting, effective login, rotation and rollback.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: A credential-changing security operation is named but Procedure/Criteria are TBD; clearing logs is incompatible with credential audit and incident evidence.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Account target, password format and protected lifecycle are core safety/operation semantics and cannot be guessed.

review_improvement: Prevents credential exposure or lockout while keeping actual password change, authentication and recovery as mandatory coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: Password mutation has irreversible incident consequences if the wrong account or encoding is used. Without protected injection and known rollback, even a syntactically valid command is unsafe; security-owner definition and approval are required before execution.
